instruction: Given a chronos gossip-flood config, predict the unique-message delivery rate and justify it.
input: star-flood gossip: 4 nodes (3 sinks), 50 msgs each, 20ms link latency, 0.0% loss, redundancy x1
output: Delivery: 150/150 = 100.0%. With 0.0% link loss and redundancy x1, every sink still receives each unique message (a star flood gives each sink 1 independent paths from the producer at x1), so delivery saturates at 100% on a lossless link. Reproducible at seed 42.

instruction: Estimate the simulated wall time for this chronos run and explain what dominates it.
input: star-flood gossip: 4 nodes (3 sinks), 50 msgs each, 20ms link latency, 0.0% loss, redundancy x1
output: Sim wall ≈ 0ms. Chronos runs in virtual time, so wall time tracks event count (150 deliveries) not real latency — the 20ms link delay is modeled, not waited on. Scale (nodes×msgs) drives wall time; latency does not.
